answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost.
